title: Enterprise Onboarding: Escalation, Integration, Support Process & QBR Playbook
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Summary

Purpose: A single, opinionated playbook for enterprise customer onboarding that combines the onboarding checklist, integration guide, escalation procedures, support process, known issues & workarounds, and QBR/health-check templates. This document is intended for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Support, and SRE teams.

Scope
- Applies to all enterprise customers onboarding onto Redwood Inference Dedicated or Private deployments and hosted customers moving to enterprise tier.
- Covers phases from pre-sales coordination to first 90 days of production, and recurring QBRs thereafter.

Ownership and Roles
- Document owner: Customer Success (owner_team).
- Primary stakeholders: CS (onboarding coordination), Solutions Engineering (integration, runbooks), Support (ticketing & triage), SRE/Platform (alerts, capacity), Account Executive (contract milestones).
- RACI (high level):
  - CS: Responsible for onboarding schedule, kickoff, and QBR cadence.
  - SE: Responsible for integration runbook and verification tests.
  - Support: Responsible for Tier 1 triage and escalation.
  - SRE: Responsible for infra health, alerts, and mitigation runbooks.

Quick links
- Standard onboarding checklist (section: Onboarding phases)
- Escalation matrix (section: Escalation playbook)
- Integration verification commands (section: Integration checks)
- QBR template and metrics (section: Health checks & QBR)

Onboarding phases (90-day plan)
1) Pre-Kickoff (contract -> kickoff meeting)
   - Deliverables: Signed SOW, contact list, initial security questionnaire, access inventory.
   - CS actions: Create onboarding Confluence page for the customer; assign CS lead; schedule 1-hour kickoff.

2) Kickoff (week 0)
   - Attendees: CS lead, SE, customer's technical lead, security contact, account owner.
   - Agenda: Objectives, success criteria, timeline, network & security constraints, data residency, escalation contacts, QBR cadence.
   - Output: Agreed milestone plan (milestone dates for integration, validation, pilot, production).

3) Integration & Validation (weeks 1-4)
   - SE provides integration guide (API keys, VPC peering, DNS, routing rules, auth).
   - Perform connectivity checks and preflight validation.
   - Run test workloads and collect baseline metrics (latency, throughput, error rate).
   - Hold weekly syncs until green.

4) Pilot (weeks 4-8)
   - Gradual traffic ramp with SLOs defined.
   - Monitor cost and performance; exercise fallback policies.
   - Validate KV caching, batching behavior, and model rollout.

5) Production & Handover (weeks 8-12)
   - Handover: SE -> Support -> CS with runbooks and run-of-show for common issues.
   - QBR schedule established (first QBR 30/60/90 day cadence then quarterly).

6) Ongoing (post-90)
   - Quarterly business reviews, model performance reviews, cost optimization suggestions.

Escalation playbook (triage & escalation matrix)
- Severity definition and target response times:
  | Severity | Impact example | Target initial response | Target remediation|
  |----------|----------------|------------------------|------------------|
  | Sev 1    | Platform outage affecting >50% of requests | 15 minutes | 4 hours (workaround) / 24 hours (full fix)|
  | Sev 2    | Partial outage, degraded latency >2x SLO | 30 minutes | 12 hours|
  | Sev 3    | Functional bug affecting small subset or non-critical feature | 4 hours | 3 business days|
  | Sev 4    | Informational / minor request | 1 business day | Next release|

- Notification channels: PagerDuty (Sev1/Sev2), Support Slack channel (#support-urgent), Email (customer and AE).
- Escalation routing:
  1. Tier 1 Support: initial triage, gather logs, verify alert thresholds, check runbooks. If unresolved in target response -> escalate to Tier 2.
  2. Tier 2 (SE + SRE): deeper diagnosis (profiling, kernel logs, infra checks). If unresolved -> escalate to Engineering on-call via PD.
  3. Engineering on-call: code or infra level fix, deploy rollback or hotfix.
  4. Exec escalation: triggered for Sev1 impacting revenue SLA or regulatory incidents.

Escalation steps (playbook)
1) Confirm and classify: collect customer ID, environment, timestamps, request IDs, affected routes, and screenshots.
2) Reproduce (if safe): use customer's isolated test tokens or staging to reproduce.
3) Baseline checks (commands & dashboards):
   - curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
   - Check model-serving dashboard: per-route P50/P95 latency, error-rate, token throughput.
   - Verify infra: kubectl -n redwood get pods; check node GPU memory and utilization.
4) Apply mitigations (examples):
   - Route traffic to fallback model variant.
   - Increase replica count (Dedicated) or expand capacity by policy.
   - Apply known workaround (see Known issues section).
5) Communicate: update ticket with status, notify AE and customer success manager, set next update cadence (15m for Sev1, 1h for Sev2).

Contact matrix (primary escalation contacts)
- Customer Success (onboarding): cs-ava@redwood.ai, +1-555-0102 (internal)
- Solutions Engineering (integration): se-solutions@redwood.ai
- Support (Tier 1): support@redwood.ai, Slack: #support-urgent
- SRE/Platform on-call: see PagerDuty schedule (link)
- Security/Legal: security@redwood.ai for incidents involving data exposure

Integration guide (technical checklist)
- Prerequisites:
  - API keys issued with correct scope; customer IPs allowlisted if required.
  - Network: VPC peering or private link configured, route tables, and NAT rules verified.
  - DNS: CNAMEs/hosts configured if private endpoint used.
  - IAM/KMS: key access tested for Private deployments.

- Integration steps (recommended):
  1. Provision API key (SE/CS action).
  2. Test authentication: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <api_key>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models | jq .
  3. Validate network path: traceroute and latency checks to the endpoint (include ports 443 & 5222 if used for sidecar).
  4. Run sample inference workload:
     - Example: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <api_key>' -d '{"model":"redwood-32b","prompt":"health-check"}'
  5. Verify KV cache behavior and warm-up: run a short prefix workload and measure subsequent P95 improvement.
  6. Validate batching: send concurrent requests to verify batching parameters and latency impact.
  7. Confirm logs and observability: customer logs forwarded to the configured destination and access rights validated.

Integration verification table (examples)
| Check | Expected result | Owner | Notes |
|-------|-----------------|-------|-------|
| Auth check | 200 + model list | SE | Ensure correct scopes |
| Health endpoint | ok + version | SRE | Match expected runtime version |
| Latency baseline | P95 < 500ms (hosted) | SE/SRE | Adjust for dedicated SLAs |
| Error rate | < 0.5% | Support | Alert if >1% for 5m |

Known issues & workarounds (living list)
1) Issue: Occasional KV cache eviction causing transient latency spikes.
   - Symptoms: Increased P95 for short bursts following long idle period.
   - Workaround: Update batching window to keep prefix warm or pre-warm KV cache by synthetic traffic during ramp windows. SE action: add pre-warm job (cron).
2) Issue: TLS handshake errors from customer proxy (mutual TLS misconfig).
   - Symptoms: 525 / handshake timeouts in logs.
   - Workaround: Validate certificate chain on both sides and disable proxy TLS inspection for Redwood endpoints. If using Private deployment, check the customer gateway TLS policy.
3) Issue: Model degradation after quantization profile applied.
   - Symptoms: reduced generation quality or repeated token repetition.
   - Workaround: Roll back to prior quantization profile or use a higher-precision variant for sensitive routes; engage Applied ML to re-evaluate quantization profile.
4) Issue: Rate-limiting on shared hosted tenant when a burst from another customer occurs.
   - Symptoms: 429s, elevated latency.
   - Workaround: Move high-throughput workloads to Dedicated or apply per-API-key rate limits and retry logic with exponential backoff.

Support process & ticket lifecycle
- Ticket intake: All customer issues should be recorded in Zendesk with product area tag (onboarding, integration, infra, billing).
- Triage: Tier 1 verifies customer environment, reproduces issue, and applies runbook steps.
- Escalation: Use the Escalation playbook above if unresolved within severity SLA.
- Communication: Templates for status updates.
  - Initial acknowledgment: "We've received your report and begun investigating. Next update in 15 minutes."
  - Post-mitigation: include root cause hypothesis, temporary mitigation, and ETA for full fix.
  - Postmortem: published for Sev1 after RCA (aim: 5 business days).

Health checks & QBR materials
- Key metrics to surface in QBRs:
  - Production request volume (tokens/sec), per-route P50/P95 latency, error rate, cost per 1M tokens, model quality metrics (precision/recall or custom evals), cache hit rates, and average batch sizes.
  - SLA adherence: uptime %, incident count, MTTR per severity.
  - Financial signals: monthly spend, projection, and savings from batching/quantization.

- QBR cadence and template:
  - 30/60/90 day QBRs during onboarding: focus on integration status, early performance, issues found, and immediate optimizations.
  - Quarterly QBRs post-onboarding: business outcomes, roadmap alignment, optimization opportunities.

QBR agenda (standard)
1. Introductions & agenda (5m)
2. Review of success criteria and current status (10m)
3. Metrics deep dive (20m)
   - Latency and error trends, model quality, cost trends, notable incidents.
4. Action items & roadmap alignment (15m)
5. Risks & open support/engineering tickets (10m)
6. Next steps and owners (5m)

Data sources for QBRs
- Redwood Console dashboards (per-route and per-model)
- Billing exports (CSV) for cost breakdowns
- Eval results from the customer prompt set (stored in Eval harness)
- Incident timelines and RCA links

Operational runbooks & artifacts to hand off
- Customer-specific runbook: includes customer IDs, API keys (redacted), permitted IP ranges, fallback model policy, and configured alerts.
- Troubleshooting checklist: common alerts and first-line mitigations.
- SLOs and error budget allocations for the customer.

Postmortem & continuous improvement
- For any Sev1 incident: produce a 5-day RCA and a 30/60/90 day action plan (owner assigned).
- Track recurring issues in regression triage board and feed into quantization/modeling backlog and runtime improvements.

Appendices
A. Example status update template
- Subject: [Customer] Incident update - {Short description} - {Sev}
- Body: What happened, Who is working on it, What we've done so far, Next update ETA, Contact info

B. Example runbook excerpt (cold-start workaround)
1) Identify affected service and route.
2) Trigger pre-warm job: POST https://api.redwood.ai/internal/prewarm -d '{"route":"/generate","prefix":"customer-warmup"}'
3) Verify P95 improves within 10 minutes.

C. Useful links
- Onboarding checklist template (Confluence)
- PagerDuty escalation schedules (internal link)
- Redwood Console dashboards (internal link)

Revision history
- 2025-11-12: Created by Ava Martinez (initial draft).
- 2026-01-20: Added integration verification table and known issues entries (reviewers: Priya Desai).
- 2026-03-04: Published with final SE and SRE review; added QBR template and runbook examples.

Notes
- This is a living document: keep known issues and contact matrix up to date. When making changes that affect runbook steps or SLAs, coordinate with SRE and Legal for any contractual implications.
